description: The request socket of one head session. A confined head cannot reach herdr, so it asks its own run supervisor, over one AF_UNIX socket the sandbox gets read-only, to perform a granted verb outside. The supervisor only transports and enforces: Identity decides who holds the role; what a persona may ask is the permission table of the session-host crate (`packages/session-host/contracts/head-permissions.v1.json`, read through `fgos_session_host::permissions` with the persona of the digest-protected envelope), and what it may write is `session.writes` of that envelope. An `fgos` argv is one frame (`fgos`): the table decides it (allow, ask or deny) and the supervisor execs the host's own `fgos` itself. `can-i` answers what the table would decide. `session bind session`, `session write`, `session save`, `fgos` and `can-i` are answered by the supervisor; every other verb is a policy branch of the Node payload behind `fgos internal head-request` (internal-route.run-supervisor.v1.json).

framing.frame: as gate-go.v1.json: 4-byte unsigned big-endian length N, then N bytes of UTF-8 JSON (one object)
framing.sizes: a request frame may be up to maxRequestBytes because `session write` carries a whole file; a reply stays within the GO channel's 65536. The length is read first: over maxRequestBytes is bad-frame; over maxReplyBytes is a large request, and while another large request is being read or run it is answered busy before its body is read. A large frame whose verb is not `session write` is bad-frame
framing.bounded: the frame is parsed with a visitor that counts every JSON value it builds (objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, null) and refuses more than maxRequestValues or nesting deeper than maxRequestDepth while it reads (bad-frame), so many tiny elements are never materialised; only one string, a session write's content, may be large
framing.oversizeOrInvalid: the supervisor answers REPLY refused bad-frame and closes the connection
framing.readDeadlineMs: 5000 for the whole request frame (not per read)

socket.kind: AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM, listening, created by the supervisor before it asks terminal-control to launch the pane
socket.path: envelope.session.requestSocketPath: a socket directly in the run supervisor's socket directory, at most 107 bytes (the same rules, the same bind helper and the same bind-back check as the GO socket)
socket.sandbox: the launch binds this one socket read-only into the head's sandbox (confinement request field requestSocket); the directory around it stays masked. Its path is also in the agent's environment as FGOS_HEAD_REQUEST_SOCKET
socket.absentWhen: the persona has no head permission table entry: no socket is created, no path is in the envelope, no variable is set
socket.lifetime: listening from before the pane launch until the gate is gone; the supervisor then unlinks the path. A client that finds the file gone reports request-socket-unavailable
socket.peerCheck: the peer uid must equal the supervisor's own (SO_PEERCRED, getpeereid elsewhere); pids are never compared. A wrong uid is answered REPLY refused peer-uid without reading a frame

fields.id: string, 1 to 64 characters of letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'
the request's id, null when no valid id was read
fields.data: object, present when done: the verb's own result
fields.message: string, optional: present only on a verb-failed refusal, the route child's own text (the reason behind its code, for example the persona names a persona-not-found lists), control characters replaced and cut to 300 characters; it may contain local paths of the same user's machine, so a client shows it only to that user

args.argv: array of strings, required, 1 to 64 words of at most 8192 bytes, none empty and none holding NUL: the `fgos` verb words and flags without the program name; no other key (bad-args)

fgos.does: the argv window, answered by the supervisor itself with no Node hop. `fgos_session_host::forwarder` screens the argv (a flag that moves the root, the cwd or the environment (`-C`, `--cwd`, `--root`, `--project`, `--env`, `--dir`, each as `--flag value` or `--flag=value`), a first word that is not an `fgos` verb word or names a shell, interpreter or raw command, and a `config patch` that is not exactly `<file> [--reason <text>]`, whose file is not a plain project-relative path outside `.fgos` without a symlink, or whose edits lie on one branch with a protected config path (one of `protectedConfigPaths` of the table, which is the one list; an edit above one counts) are refused `argv-not-allowed` for every persona; the host is given a private copy of the bytes the window checked, never the caller's path, and the copy is removed after the call) and asks the permission table (`packages/session-host/contracts/head-permissions.v1.json`) with the persona of the envelope (`session.persona`, else the persona `session.role` spells). `allow` on a forward row: the supervisor execs the envelope's host `fgos` with the argv plus `--json` (and the row's `append`), from envelope.cwd, with exactly the step environment, no shell, inside the verb timeout, and returns the host's JSON `data`, or the host's own refusal code with its message. `allow` on a `node` or `native` row: refused `argv-not-allowed` (that verb is sent as the frame of its own name, which keeps its policy branch). `ask`, including an argv no row matches: one five-part owner question carrying the exact argv is filed through `fgos internal head-questions` and the reply is refused `asked` with the question id as detail; nothing ran. `deny`: refused `argv-not-allowed` with the reason in detail
fgos.identity: held (the successor's read rows only: the rows the table marks `read: true`, which a rotation successor may use before it holds the role)
fgos.rule: refusals: argv-not-allowed, recipient-not-allowed (a `--to` outside the values of the persona's `mailbox send` row), asked, bad-args, verb-timeout, reply-too-large, and the host verb's own code carried as it is (for example event-store-no-repository, session-not-found)

args.argv: array of strings, required, as for fgos

can-i.does: answered by the supervisor itself: the decision the table and the forwarder's refusals give the argv for this caller's persona, from the same function a real call uses. It runs nothing, files nothing and takes no busy slot; a rotation successor may ask it before it holds the role
can-i.data: {decision: allow | ask | deny, reason: one line naming the row or the refusal}

args.name: string, required
args.beside: string, optional: the live key of the session whose tab the new one opens next to
args.forQuestion: string, optional: the id of an owner question the new head continues (1 to 64 characters of letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'); the opening text gains one line naming it, and the successor, which holds the asker's own head role, writes the answer back and acks or cancels it

session start.does: startHeadSession (src/session-host/head-start.mjs) in the project of the attempt's envelope (envelope.cwd); a live head of the same role is fronted instead of started
session start.data: the object startHeadSession returns ({already, role, key, ...})

args.name: string, required; with persona it must spell the envelope's own role (head:<persona>-<name>), otherwise role-mismatch: a head asks for its own lineage only
args.reason: soft | hard | manual, required; `none` only together with `measure` (a stop that measured below soft: it is recorded and nothing is rotated)
args.stopFacts: object, optional: sessionId, portfolio (at most 50 paths), delta, lastAssistantMessage, pendingQuestion (strings of at most 8000 characters); anything else is refused bad-stop-facts
args.measure: object, optional: fraction (number or null), source (sidecar | transcript | null), stale (boolean), decision (the decision reason, at most 60 characters); anything else is refused bad-measure. Every stop of a head sends it, and the host appends one line with the request outcome to the lineage's stop-trace.jsonl (newest 500 lines kept once it passes 256 KiB)

session rotate.does: requestRotation (src/session-rotation/rotate.mjs), the one entry that asks for a rotation (`fgos session rotate` calls the same one): checks the request, writes it under the lineage folder and starts the executor `rotateHeadSession` as a detached process through the detach door, then returns at once; the executor outlives the verb timeout
session rotate.data: {started: true, pid} or {started: false, reason: rotation-in-progress | spawn-failed | below-threshold}

args.name: string, required; spelled as the envelope's own role, as for session rotate

session restore role.does: nothing in the route child (it only checks the arguments); the effect is the supervisor's: after the child reports done it registers the envelope's role for this attempt's session again, WITHOUT take. Used by the rotation executor when a failed rotation left no live session holding the role (a late take landed on the ended successor): Identity refuses role-held when any live session holds it, so a restore never displaces a holder
session restore role.rule: same role step as session answered (this attempt's own session is registered and live, session-not-registered otherwise); a refused registration is role-take-failed with Identity's code in detail. The executor reaches this socket as the same user (peer uid)

args.ref: string, optional: what the question is about (plan:<dir>[#phase-<nn>], ...); the checkout it is checked in is the envelope's cwd
args.supersedes: string, optional: the id of this head's own earlier question to cancel when the new one is written

questions ask.does: the host route `fgos internal head-questions --run-dir <attemptDir>` (apps/fgos/src/wiring/head_questions.rs), reached through the Node payload: it reads envelope.json itself and runs the fgos-questions use case with the asker taken from the envelope (the role from envelope.session.role, the session, handle, roles and machine from Identity as the holder of that role, the persona from the envelope, the project from envelope.cwd). No argument names a caller; a `role`, `asker` or `by` key in args is dropped
questions ask.rule: the same role step as session rotate (role-not-held otherwise); the use case's refusals come back as verb-failed with its code in detail (for example ref-invalid, parts-incomplete, question-unclear, asker-unresolved)

questions ack.does: as questions ask: records that the asker received the answer; only the asker or a holder of the asker's head role may close a question
questions ack.rule: refusals: question-unknown, not-asker, question-not-open (carried as verb-failed detail)

args.reason: string, required by the use case

questions cancel.does: as questions ask: cancels the head's own open question

args.option: string, optional: the label of one of the question's options
args.text: string, optional; one of option and text is required

questions answer.does: as questions ask, with source `secretary`: records the owner's answer (by: owner) that the secretary head carries. Granted to the secretary only; the route refuses it for any other head with answer-not-owner whatever the grant said
questions answer.rule: refusals: answer-not-owner, question-already-answered, question-not-open, question-unknown (carried as verb-failed detail)

args.source: string, required: the CLI's own session variable the agent names itself by (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CODEX_THREAD_ID, PI_SESSION_ID), never FGOS_SESSION_ID
args.value: string, required: the agent's session id under that variable
args.mailbox: object {fgosDir, name}, optional, both strings: the mailbox name the agent's hooks bound in the project of fgosDir, recorded as the bound entry's Identity `mailbox` group; no other key is accepted

session bind session.does: answered by the supervisor itself, no route child: Identity's bind_agent_session registers the agent session on the attempt's gate and moves every role the attempt holds to it (take), with the `terminal` and `head` identifier groups, so the head resolves as its CLI session and a role alias reaches the mailbox key its hooks bind. The bound entry also records its `cliSession` group (the variable and id; for CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID also the name, name source, messaging socket, pid and start time the CLI keeps in `<config dir>/sessions/<agent pid>.json` outside the sandbox, read only when that file names the agent's pid, the bound id and the agent's start time; the agent is the gate's direct child above the connecting process) and the `mailbox` group of the args. A bind of the session already bound refreshes these groups. The connecting process (SO_PEERCRED pid, as the supervisor's PID namespace names it) must be the gate or run under it; Identity refuses an attempt with no live entry on the gate and an agent id that is a live session on another head. Afterwards the role checks of this socket ask for the session the attempt is (the bound one when there is one) and a role move registers on it
session bind session.rule: the role step is the registered one of session answered (a successor binds before it holds the role); a refused bind is session-bind-failed with Identity's code in detail (bad-args, peer-unknown, gate-unknown, invalid-writer-key, caller-not-under-head, agent-not-gate-child, attempt-not-registered, session-in-use, head-not-live, ...). The mailbox hook of a confined head sends it the first time it binds a head, instead of writing Identity's read-only directory

args.path: string, required: project-relative, exactly an entry of envelope.session.writes
args.content: string, required: the whole new content (UTF-8)
args.base: string, optional: the git blob id (40 or 64 lowercase hex) of the file content the writer read and based the edit on; no other keys

session write.does: answered by the supervisor itself, no route child: the only way a head changes a granted file, because its sandbox keeps every granted file read-only (granted directories stay bound writable). The path must be plain and relative (no empty, `.` or `..` segment, not absolute: path-invalid), named exactly by an entry of envelope.session.writes (path-not-granted), and an existing regular file reached from envelope.cwd without a symlink at it or at any directory on the way (path-symlink, not-a-file). Its directory is opened once, no-follow at every component, and the content is installed through that descriptor by the durable-file door (Dir::replace: temp file beside it given exactly the old file's mode, fsync, renameat over the name, directory fsync), so nothing is resolved by path after the check and a directory swapped meanwhile is never followed; a reader sees the old or the new file, never a mix; a failure there is write-failed with the step in detail. The write goes through the existing paths land (`fgos_supervision::land`, through one port, WritePublisher, that the composition root apps/fgos fills in wiring/session_write_publish.rs and passes to the supervisor route as a parameter; this crate commits, fetches and pushes nothing), in this order: (0) the land's own first step alone (`land::catch_up`): under the target's merge slot the main checkout is fast-forwarded to the remote tip; a checked-out branch with commits its remote lacks is refused write-branch-ahead, a catch-up Git marks Busy (its retryable class: resource-busy while a live writer's operation is pending, worktree-admin-held, merge-slot-busy, main-checkout-busy, repo-config-busy) is retried with bounded backoff (45 s of retries; the last attempt may itself wait a few seconds per lock, so about 60 s at most, far inside the client's 180 s write reply timeout; the 60 s verb timeout bounds route children, not this request) and, if it stays Busy, answered write-busy naming the last code, never write-catch-up-refused; any other catch-up refusal write-catch-up-refused; (1) the path must have no uncommitted change in the main checkout (write-path-dirty; write-path-unreadable when that cannot be read); (1b) the base check: the expected content is the request's `base`, else the blob id the file had when the request arrived (before the catch-up); a current blob id (read after the catch-up and the clean check, through the Git port) that differs is refused write-base-stale with both ids in the detail, so an edit built from an older copy never replaces newer rows; (2) the atomic write; (3) the paths land: only that path is committed with the subject `docs(<role>): write <path>` (role = envelope.session.role, writer = envelope.identity.writerId), and the checked-out branch is pushed without force. Every refusal before (2) leaves nothing written. Gates run only for the paths their `when` matches (a configured gate list whose globs match none of the path runs nothing); they run inside this request, under the client's 180 s bound, and the busy flag is held meanwhile. A land refusal is not a refusal of the request: the reply is done with `publish` naming it, and nothing is forced. Its true outcome: a push the remote rejects (it moved after the sync) undoes the land's own unpublished commit through the Git door (undo_unpublished_commit: the branch and index return to the commit's parent, every byte stays) and starts over from a fresh sync, at most 3 more times, then land-retries-exhausted; land-commit-contract-violation (a hook changed the commit) and a footprint refusal undo the commit the same way, so a refusal never leaves the branch ahead of its remote and the next write is not refused write-branch-ahead; every other land refusal leaves the file written and uncommitted
session write.peer: the connecting process (SO_PEERCRED pid) must be the attempt's gate or run under it, the check of session bind session (Identity's caller_under_head): a same-uid process outside the head is refused caller-not-under-gate. The other verbs check the role only: session start, session rotate, session answered and session restore role act on the caller's own lineage or ask the use case to check it, so they are not given this check here
session write.data: {path, bytes, commit} when published, or {path, bytes, publish: {refusal, detail}} when written but not published (refusal is the land refusal code, e.g. land-retries-exhausted or land-commit-contract-violation with the file written and uncommitted, land-gate-failed or land-gate-missing with the file uncommitted)
session write.client: `fgos session write <path> [--base <oid>]` with the new content on stdin; no --base sends the blob id of the file as it is on disk (src/session-host/head-request-client.mjs requestHeadWrite)

args.paths: array of strings, required, non-empty: project-relative paths, each inside an entry of envelope.session.writes

session save.does: answered by the supervisor itself, no route child: commits exactly the named paths on the checked-out branch of the head's working checkout (the attempt cwd, which must be a linked worktree of the project) through ScopedCommit. The working checkout must not be the main checkout (save-needs-linked-worktree). Every path must lie inside envelope.session.writes (path-outside-grant): equal to a granted entry or beneath it, so the directory grant plans/discussions covers plans/discussions/<dir>/DISCUSSION.md. The paths are the head's own edits already in the working checkout; only the named paths that changed are committed and any other change stays uncommitted. When none of the named paths has a change relative to HEAD it answers save-nothing-to-commit. Main's tip is untouched in every case.
session save.peer: the connecting process (SO_PEERCRED pid) must be the attempt's gate or run under it, the check of session bind session and session write (caller-not-under-gate)

args.name: string, required; spelled as the envelope's own role, as for session rotate
args.sessionId: string, required: the successor's Identity session id
args.rotationId: string, required: 16 lowercase hex characters, the id of the pending rotation exactly as the handoff's `Rotation id:` line carries it; the successor reads it from its handoff and echoes it, no other match is made
args.message: string, required: the successor's first assistant message, kept as evidence, at most 8000 characters

session answered.does: markSuccessorAnswered (src/session-rotation/rotate.mjs): records the answer of the successor the lineage's pending rotation waits for. The key is the attempt's own (envelope.unitRunId), never an argument. Refused no-rotation-pending when no rotation waits for that key (the executor removes its pending record before it gives up, so a late answer is refused), answer-mismatch when rotationId is not exactly the pending rotation's id; this is the one place an answer is checked
session answered.rule: the one verb of a rotation successor, which does not hold the role yet: the supervisor's role step asks Identity only that this attempt's own session is registered and live (session-not-registered otherwise), and after the route child reports done the supervisor moves the envelope's role to this session with Identity's take (register_writer, take) against the gate it launched; a failed move is role-take-failed. The role never moves on a refused answer. Identity stays the only authority for who holds a role; the supervisor only transports the fact that the attempt is that session

args.branch: string, optional: a branch to land; a lead only (land-branch-lead-only for any other persona)
args.paths: array of strings, optional: exact main-checkout paths to commit; every one must lie inside an entry of envelope.session.writes (path-outside-grant)
args.tests: array of strings, optional: test paths for a gate that uses {tests}; sent to the host as one --test <path> per path
args.message: string, optional: the commit message; required with paths

land.does: answers at once with a ticket (the request id): the route child writes the ticket file and starts a detached runner that runs the host verb `fgos land --json` to its end and rewrites the ticket; `request result` reads it. Exactly one of branch and paths; any other key is bad-args, and so is any string that becomes one argv token (branch, message, paths, tests) and starts with '-'. A lead's branch land passes the footprint of its plan, read from plan.md at the trunk tip, as --footprint, and is refused write-outside-footprint when the plan has none; a lead's paths land that would change that footprint in the plan's own plan.md is refused footprint-change-refused
land.rule: refusals (verb-failed detail): bad-args, land-branch-lead-only, path-outside-grant, write-outside-footprint, footprint-change-refused, ticket-used, plan-not-found, plan-ambiguous

run.routeHost: which host the route child is, for this verb and every other verb that runs the Node payload: the active release's host. A head launched from an activated release (its start host lies inside the release that was active at launch) resolves the project's current activation again on every request and runs that release's host and its manifest payload, so a head that outlives a release switch picks the new release up without a restart. The handover is verified in the child: the running host must be the activated host and the payload a manifest-relative directory inside that same release, otherwise the child refuses host-version-mismatch; no request argument names either path. This is the head-request route only: attempt steps stay pinned to the host their envelope names. A head launched from a dev start host (one outside an activated release) is never switched. When the activation cannot be read, is not ready, or names no executable host inside its release, the request runs on the start host and the supervisor logs one line, `head-request <id> release-fallback: <why>`.

args.prompt: string, required; must not start with '-'
args.provider: string, optional; must not start with '-'
args.capability: string, optional; must not start with '-'
args.writes: array of strings, optional: each must be contained in the lead's plan footprint by the repo's write-scope semantics (write-outside-footprint); `src/**` is not contained in `src/*`
args.worktree: string, optional: a linked worktree; must not start with '-'
args.maxMinutes: integer, optional, the two coordinators only: wall-clock minutes of the unit (--timeout), at most secretary.run.maxMinutes (default 15, the ceiling); the default is the ceiling
args.tier: string, optional, the two coordinators only: the unit's tier (--override), at most secretary.run.tier (default standard)

run.does: a lead, or the secretary under the ceilings below. A lead: a `unit` key is bad-args (a unit file declares its own writes, which the footprint could not bound). Answers at once with a ticket as land does; the detached runner runs `fgos run --json` without FGOS_DISPATCH_DEPTH (a lead's phase run is a top-level seat and takes a lane) and the ticket keeps only the unitRunId, whose outcome stays in .fgos/assignments/<unitRunId>/ The secretary's run is one unit built from a prompt: no provider, capability, unit file or plan footprint of hers; read-only unless `writes` names plain project-relative paths and `worktree` is a linked worktree of this project (absolute, not the project checkout, its `.git` a file); it runs `fgos run <prompt> --timeout <maxMinutes>m --override {"tier":<tier>}` and a request may ask for less than `secretary.run.maxMinutes` and `secretary.run.tier`, never more. The ticket and `request result` work as a lead's.
run.rule: refusals (verb-failed detail): bad-args, role-mismatch (not a lead), write-outside-footprint, ticket-used, plan-not-found, plan-ambiguous; the secretary also: run-one-unit (a unit or units key), run-ceiling-exceeded (maxMinutes or tier above secretary.run.*), writes-need-linked-worktree

args.worktree: string: the absolute path of a linked worktree of this project, as `git worktree list` of the project root names it (not the main checkout); no other key (bad-args)

release check.does: answered by the supervisor itself, no route child: writes the ticket where `request result` reads it (`.fgos/runtime/head-tickets/<role>/<id>.json`; a second ticket with the id is ticket-used) and answers at once; a detached thread then runs each `release.checks` argv of the project's recipe, with no shell, unconfined, with the worktree as its working directory, and rewrites the ticket. It runs only the checks: no apply, probe, rollback, merge-slot look, check checkout, release record or release lock, so it may run beside a release and changes nothing on main. Every check runs, so the result names every red one; no checks is green with a note
release check.result: `request result <id>` reads the ticket: state done with `result` {green: boolean, checks: [{argv, exit, error?}], note?} (a red check is an answer, not a failure: state stays done and `result` is carried with green false, and the ticket also carries a non-zero `exit`, the first red check's own exit or 1 when that argv could not be run, so `request result` shows a non-zero exit; a check's `exit` is null with `error` when the argv could not be run), or failed with code `recipe-invalid`
release check.grant: the lead only; every other persona is refused verb-not-granted
release check.rule: refusals (verb-failed detail): bad-args, worktree-not-registered (the path is not a linked worktree of this project), ticket-used

args.rollback: boolean, optional: true runs only the recipe's `rollback` (the secretary's path when the supervisor does not come back after a release); no other key (bad-args)

release run.does: answered by the supervisor itself, no route child: writes the ticket where `request result` reads it (`.fgos/runtime/head-tickets/<role>/<id>.json`, the id the request's; a second ticket with the id is ticket-used) and answers at once; a detached thread then runs `fgos_session_host::release` against the project's `release.*` recipe and rewrites the ticket. In order: no `apply` is `no-recipe`; a trunk tip equal to the trunk commit the last `released` outcome recorded in `.fgos/runtime/release/state.json` is `nothing-new` (with no record the trunk counts as new; the host's version is never consulted); a land holding the merge slot, or a slot whose status is unknown, is `land-in-progress`, looked at again right before apply; each `checks` argv, in an exact checkout of the trunk tip (none is made when there are no checks; a checkout that cannot be made ends `check-checkout-failed` with nothing run), the first non-zero is `checks-failed`; a recipe that is not `reversible` files one owner question (Apply or Do not apply) with the exact `apply` argv and ends `asked` without applying; otherwise `apply`, then `probe`, and a failed apply or probe runs `rollback` and ends `rolled-back` (`rollback-failed` when that fails too); `apply` and `probe` are each written into the state record as the step in progress before they run, and every terminal outcome of the run clears it; a `released` outcome writes the trunk commit it released (atomic temp and rename). One report line (information, no choice) goes to the owner through the question store for every outcome that changed or refused something, `land-in-progress`, `checks-failed` and `rollback-failed` included; an `ask-failed` run, whose question route just failed, writes one clear line to the supervisor log instead. `{rollback: true}` refuses `no-release-in-flight` unless the state record shows a step that never ended (the flock being free, the run that wrote it is dead). One release runs at a time across both personas, the rollback included: a kernel flock (exclusive, non-blocking, close-on-exec) on `.fgos/runtime/release/lock`, held by the supervisor for the whole run, refuses a second request `release-in-progress`; the kernel frees it when the supervisor dies. The ticket's `runner` is the supervisor's process identity, so a supervisor that ends mid-run reads `runner-gone`; recipe argv die with the supervisor (lock, runner and children share one lifetime; `fgctl upgrade` publishes the activation by temp file and rename, so a killed upgrade leaves the old or the new release) and write to `<id>.log` beside the ticket. The ticket is written atomically. The checks run with no shell in an exact checkout of the trunk tip (made through `fgos worktree create --detach --base <tip>` under `<project>-worktrees/release-check-<id>`, holding the tip's committed `.fgos`, each check with no inherited `FGOS_*` variable and `TMPDIR` set to `<checkout>/.fgos/runtime/tmp`, removed with `fgos worktree remove --delivered-to <tip> --discard-ignored` after the checks, a refused removal reported, not fatal); `apply`, `probe` and `rollback` run with no shell from the project root. The host is asked for `config show --path release` and `lock-status`; the recipe is project data (`core/config-standard/release.yaml`) and never read by the skills
release run.result: `request result <id>` reads the ticket: state done (`released`, `asked`) or failed with code `no-recipe`, `nothing-new`, `land-in-progress`, `check-checkout-failed`, `checks-failed`, `rolled-back`, `recipe-invalid`, `rollback-failed`, `no-release-in-flight` or another step code, and `result` holding the outcome
release run.grant: the supervisor and, by inheritance, the secretary; every other persona is refused verb-not-granted

args.id: string, optional: a ticket of this role
args.wait: number, optional: seconds to wait for a running ticket to end, at most 50

request result.does: reads this role's own tickets in the role's own ticket folder under .fgos/runtime. With id, that ticket (ticket-unknown for another role's or a missing one); without id, the role's tickets, newest first. A running ticket whose runner record judges dead reads state failed, code runner-gone; an unknown judgement stays running
request result.data: {id, verb, state: running|done|failed, argv, exit?, code?, message?, stderrTail?, result?, unitRunId?} for one ticket; argv is the host argv built from the request fields (never secrets); on a failed run code is the host's own refusal code when it gave one (else exit-N), message its refusal text (at most 1 KB) and stderrTail the last stderr lines (bounded), {tickets: [...]} without id

args.branch: string, required (a detached worktree is not this door's: bad-args without it)

worktree create.does: lead only. Runs the host verb `fgos worktree create <path> --branch <branch> [--base <base>]` within the verb limit and returns its answer
worktree create.data: the host verb's JSON, or {created: true}
worktree create.rule: refusals (verb-failed detail): bad-args, role-mismatch (not a lead), worktree-create-failed

session stop.does: stopHeadSession (src/session-host/head-stop.mjs): ends the live head the way a rotation ends the old head (writes retiredAt into the lineage's placement.json first, asks the head's own supervisor to stop it, waits for its attempt to close, then retires the pane through Session Host; a head that does not end is stop-not-ended and keeps its record), and retiredAt is what the head-state source reads as retired. Refused role-mismatch unless the persona-name is a lead or planner lineage of this project, the asker of an answered question, or the caller's own role The secretary and the supervisor may stop any head, and a target persona that holds no head grant is refused stop-target-not-head for them (a hand-started session is not stopped here).
session stop.rule: refusals (verb-failed detail): role-mismatch, stop-not-ended, retire-refused, bad-persona, bad-name, stop-target-not-head

supervisor done.does: as supervisor handled, running `fgos supervisor done --json`; when the answer is {done: true} the route, after its line is written, starts a detached `session stop` of the caller's own role and adds stopping: true
supervisor done.data: the host verb's JSON data, with stopping: true when the caller's own stop was started
supervisor done.rule: refusals (verb-failed detail): the host verb's own code (events still unhandled)

args.plan: string, required: the plan directory name; must match the caller's own plan from envelope role (plan-not-own); must not start with '-'
args.phase: string, required: the phase id to widen; must not start with '-'
args.path: string, optional: a repo-relative path to add to the footprint; repeatable or as paths
args.paths: array of strings, optional: repo-relative paths to add to the footprint; at least one path or paths is required
args.criterion: integer, required: the 1-based number of the acceptance criterion this widening serves; at least 1

supervisor widen.does: answers at once with a ticket (the request id) as land does: the route child writes the ticket file and starts a detached runner that runs the host verb `fgos supervisor widen <plan> --phase <phase> --path <paths...> --criterion <criterion> --json` to its end and rewrites the ticket; `request result` reads it. A lead only; resolves the caller's own plan from the envelope role (`planOfHead`) and refuses `plan-not-own` when the plan argument differs. Any other key is bad-args, and so is any string that becomes one argv token and starts with '-'. The lead's write grant is not widened
supervisor widen.rule: refusals (verb-failed detail): bad-args, role-mismatch (not a lead), plan-not-own, ticket-used, plan-not-found, plan-not-widenable, phase-not-found, criterion-not-found, footprint-entry-invalid

args.records: array of 1 to 10 record objects, required: observe.record.v2 objects whose `kind` is `fgos.coordination.*`; v, id, ts, basis and origin may be left out as for `fgos metrics record`. The request frame's own bounds (256 values, depth 8) apply to the whole array

metrics record.does: as supervisor handled, running `fgos metrics record --json -` with the records on stdin: the fail-open record door of Observe, limited to coordination evidence. Any record of another kind refuses the whole call, nothing written. From inside a confined head `fgos metrics record --json -` sends its stdin through this verb
metrics record.data: the host verb's JSON data ({written, duplicate, rejected, failed, outcomes})
metrics record.rule: refusals (verb-failed detail): bad-args, kind-not-allowed (a record's kind is not fgos.coordination.*)

questionsRoute.argv: `<hostBin> internal head-questions --run-dir <attemptDir>`, one request on stdin, `{"v":1,"verb":"questions ask|ack|cancel|answer","args":{...}}`
questionsRoute.answer: one stdout line, `{"result":"done","data":{...}}` or `{"result":"error","code":"<code>","message":"..."}`; exit 0 or 70
questionsRoute.owner: apps/fgos main.rs dispatches it before the route table, beside seat-binding (it is not in command-routes.json or help); internal-route.run-supervisor.v1.json and route.rs stay the supervisor's own routes
questionsRoute.caller: the Node payload (runHeadRequest) calls it for the four questions verbs and returns its line unchanged; inside a head the `fgos questions` write sub-verbs send these verbs through this socket when FGOS_HEAD_REQUEST_SOCKET is set, retrying a busy reply 3 times, 1 s apart; reads go straight to the store

order: role: Identity resolves the role to the live session it names and that session must be this attempt's own (role-not-held otherwise, including when Identity cannot answer: the request fails closed; role-pending-rotation instead when the live holder is this head's own earlier generation; a read row of the permission table or `can-i` from such a successor is answered instead, from the same Identity fact and nothing in the request, while every other verb keeps role-pending-rotation). For `session answered`, `session restore role` and `session bind session` the step is instead: this attempt's own session is registered and live (session-not-registered, failing closed the same way)
verb: a policy verb must be a `node` or `native` row the persona's rules allow (verb-not-granted); `fgos` and `can-i` ask the table about the argv instead (argv-not-allowed, asked)
peer (session write and session save): the connecting process runs under the gate (caller-not-under-gate)
busy: at most one request runs at a time (busy)

run: `<hostBin> internal head-request --protocol 1 --run-dir <attemptDir>`, request on stdin; `session bind session`, `session write`, `session save`, `fgos` and `can-i` are answered by the supervisor itself instead

run.child: started with exactly the step environment of the envelope, the envelope's cwd, its own process group, and the parent-death signal on Linux; stdout is its one JSON line, stderr goes to supervisor.log
run.onTimeout: the child's process group is killed and the reply is refused verb-timeout (the head's own launch waits up to 45 s for its binding)
run.childLine: {"v":1,"protocol":1,"result":"done","data":{...}} or {"result":"error","code":"<the entry's code>","message":"..."}; an exit with no such line is detail `the route ended with exit N`
run.never: the tick of the supervisor never waits on a request: every connection is served on its own thread, at most 8 at once (a further one is closed unanswered)

refusalCodes.peer-uid: the connection is not from the supervisor's own user
refusalCodes.plan-not-own: supervisor widen only: a lead naming a plan directory other than its own
refusalCodes.bad-frame: oversize, not one JSON object, no REQUEST type, an id outside the rule, a verb that is not a string or args that is not an object
refusalCodes.role-not-held: Identity does not give this attempt's session the envelope's role; when Identity could not answer the detail is its refusal code only (its text goes to supervisor.log, never to the client)
refusalCodes.role-pending-rotation: a role-gated verb from a rotation successor (same persona and name as the live holder, a higher generation) whose role its live predecessor still holds, the move of `session answered` or `session restore role` not done yet; detail names the predecessor. Retryable: every client (the JS `requestHead` and the Rust `head_client::request_head`) waits with doubling backoff (0.5 s up to 4 s) for at most 60 s, then reports the code; the rotation stop hook passes no wait. The read rows of the permission table (`read: true`, `questions`) and `can-i` are exempt: a pending successor gets them answered; every write verb keeps this refusal. Any other caller without the role stays role-not-held
refusalCodes.verb-not-granted: a policy verb (a frame of its own name) that the persona's rows of the permission table do not allow; detail names the verb, the role and the persona
refusalCodes.recipient-not-allowed: fgos only: a `mailbox send` whose `--to` lies outside the values of the persona's `mailbox send` row; detail is the reason
refusalCodes.argv-not-allowed: fgos only:the argv is refused: a flag that moves the root, the cwd or the environment, a first word that is not an fgos verb, a config patch that is not the exact shape or touches a protected config path, a row that denies it, a verb that belongs to a policy frame, a flag value outside the row's `args` or `limits`, a session target that is not a plain role, handle or slot key, or a persona the table does not name; detail is the reason
refusalCodes.asked: fgos only: no row decides the argv, so one owner question carrying it was filed and nothing ran; detail is the question id
refusalCodes.busy: another request is running, or another large request (over maxReplyBytes) is being read or run
refusalCodes.session-not-registered: session answered only: Identity does not list this attempt's own session as live; when Identity could not answer the detail is its refusal code only
refusalCodes.session-bind-failed: session bind session only: Identity refused to bind the session; detail is its code
refusalCodes.bad-args: the args of a verb break its contract shape: for session write not {path, content} and optionally base, all strings, or a base that is not a 40 or 64 digit lowercase hex blob id; for session save not non-empty string paths array and non-empty string message; for any other verb a missing, unknown or mistyped key, or a string that becomes a host argv token and starts with '-'
refusalCodes.path-invalid: session write and session save: the path is empty, absolute, or has an empty, `.` or `..` segment
refusalCodes.path-not-granted: session write only: no entry of envelope.session.writes names the path exactly
refusalCodes.path-symlink: session write only: the file or a directory on the way to it is a symbolic link
refusalCodes.not-a-file: session write only: the granted path does not exist or is not a regular file (a granted directory is written in the sandbox, not here)
refusalCodes.caller-not-under-gate: session write and session save: the connecting process is not the attempt's gate nor one of its descendants; detail is Identity's code (caller-not-under-head, head-not-live) or gate-unknown, peer-unknown
refusalCodes.write-branch-ahead: session write only: the main checkout's branch has commits its remote lacks (an earlier write was committed but not pushed); nothing was written; detail names both tips
refusalCodes.write-busy: session write only: the catch-up stayed Busy (a live writer's Git operation pending, the merge slot or the main checkout held) through its bounded retries; retryable, nothing was written; detail is `<land refusal code>: <detail>`; retry the write later
refusalCodes.write-catch-up-refused: session write only: the main checkout could not be fast-forwarded to its remote tip; nothing was written; detail is `<land refusal code>: <detail>`, e.g. main-checkout-catch-up-refused, resource-recovery-required, land-remote-outcome-unknown
refusalCodes.write-base-stale: session write only: the file is not the content the write was based on (the request's base, else what the file held when the request arrived, which the catch-up may have moved); nothing was written; detail names the current and the given blob id; read the file again, redo the edit, write again
refusalCodes.write-path-dirty: session write only: the path already has an uncommitted change in the main checkout; nothing was written
refusalCodes.write-path-unreadable: session write only: the state of the path in the main checkout could not be read; nothing was written; detail names why
refusalCodes.write-failed: session write only: the durable write failed; detail names the error and the step (a failure after the rename means the new content may already be in place)
refusalCodes.role-take-failed: session answered only: the route recorded the answer but Identity refused to move the role to this session (detail is its code, for example gate-unknown or head-not-live); the executor then finds no holder change and retires the successor
refusalCodes.save-needs-linked-worktree: session save only: attempt cwd is not a linked worktree (cannot save to the main checkout; use session write instead)
refusalCodes.save-failed: session save only: the commit could not be made; detail is `<git refusal code>: <detail>`; nothing was committed
refusalCodes.save-nothing-to-commit: session save only: working tree and index have no changes relative to HEAD for the specified paths
refusalCodes.release-in-progress: release run only: another release run (either persona, the rollback included) holds the release flock
refusalCodes.ticket-used: land and run only: a ticket with the request id already exists for this role
refusalCodes.ticket-unknown: request result only: the role has no ticket with that id
refusalCodes.land-branch-lead-only: land only: a branch land asked by a persona that is not a lead
refusalCodes.path-outside-grant: land and session save: a path that lies in no entry of envelope.session.writes
refusalCodes.write-outside-footprint: run only: a writes path the lead's plan footprint (read at the trunk tip) does not cover
refusalCodes.footprint-change-refused: land only: a lead's paths land that changes the footprint of its own plan's plan.md against the trunk tip; the widen verb is the one door a lead changes its footprint through
refusalCodes.verb-failed: the route child failed; detail is the entry's own code (for example head-key-used, bad-persona, start-refused) or the exit
refusalCodes.verb-timeout: the verb ran longer than verbTimeoutMs
refusalCodes.reply-too-large: the verb answered, but its data does not fit one reply frame (maxReplyBytes); the detail names the size. A route child that sees a host answer over its own bound refuses with this code too

envelope.refusal: envelope-invalid (the supervisor refuses the attempt before the pane is launched)
rules: session.persona (else the persona session.role spells) names no persona of the head permission table while session.requestSocketPath is present
session.writes present and not an array of strings
the socket path lies in the very directory of the attempt's GO socket (envelope.terminal.socketPath): the same rule the sandbox bind-back applies on its side
identity.writerId, session.role and hostBin are non-empty strings
at least one process step (not a builtin) exists: the route child starts with the environment of the first one and nothing else

trust: the route reads the attempt's own run directory and its envelope as trusted because the sandbox only ever sees it read-only. The guard is the paths grant: a workspace-paths entry under `.fgos` is refused by name (confinement shape, validateWorkspacePaths), so no grant can make that directory writable
log: one line per request in supervisor.log: `head-request <id> <verb> <done|refused> <code|->`; arguments are never logged and client text is cut to 32 plain characters
client: src/session-host/head-request.mjs: `requestHeadStart` connects to FGOS_HEAD_REQUEST_SOCKET after checking the socket file is owned by its own uid; `requestHead(verb, args)` is the one client; `startHead` and `rotateHead` are the one branch per verb (FGOS_CONFINED=1 asks through the socket, refused no-request-socket when the variable is unset, otherwise startHeadSession or requestRotation directly); `requestHeadAnswered` is the successor's call; every other policy verb goes through the generic `requestHead(verb, args)` with the constants of head-request-client.mjs; every forward-only verb (`session read|type`, `watcher tune`, `supervisor raise|handled|queue|plans|wake`, `slots`, `questions` list, `metrics prune`, `friction record`, `config patch`) and `can-i` are sent by the Rust `fgos` as one `fgos` or `can-i` frame carrying the caller's own argv. A long verb (`land`, `run`) answers a ticket at once, because the socket serves one request at a time and caps a verb at verbTimeoutMs; its detached runner outlives the route child
